 Vajiram & Ravi provides Daily UPSC Prelims Current Affairs for 3 November 2026, tailored for aspirants. We cover all relevant news and events crucial for the exam, ensuring you stay updated & well-prepared.
 Teghaza 001: 4.1-Billion-Year-Old Mars Meteorite Found in Sahara Desert 
 November 3, 2026 
 Teghaza 001 Latest News 
 A rose-coloured meteorite discovered in the Sahara Desert in 2022 named Teghaza 001 has turned out to be one of the oldest pieces of Mars ever found on Earth. 
 About Teghaza 001 
 It is a rose-coloured meteorite discovered in the Sahara Desert in 2022 .   
 The meteorite was named after the Teghaza salt plain in Mali , where it was discovered. 
 It is among roughly 435 Martian meteorites identified on Earth and is considered one of the three most ancient samples of the Red Planet found so far. 
 The other two among the three most ancient Martian meteorites found on Earth are ALH84001 and a sample nicknamed Black Beauty.   
 The meteorite weighs nearly 800 grams.  
 It dates back more than 4.1 billion yea rs, when the mineral zircon crystallized from molten magma on Mars.  
 Because zircon allows exceptionally precise radiometric dating, this immediately placed the meteorite alongside the two other Martian remnants of a similar age.  
 Analysis showed that Teghaza 001’s texture and composition do not match any other known meteorite group.   
 What impressed researchers most was the presence of chemical markers indicating that the rock had been in contact with liquid water during its formation and evolution.  
 This makes Teghaza 001 a direct witness to an era when Mars was wet and potentially suitable for life to emerge.  
 Meteoroid, a meteor, or meteorite? 
 Meteoroids : Meteoroids are bits of solid material of different sizes orbiting the Sun.   
 Meteors When meteoroids enter Earth’s atmosphere (or that of another planet, like Mars) at high speed and burn up , the fireballs, or “shooting stars,” are called meteors. 
 Meteorites: When a meteoroid survives a trip through the atmosphere and hits the ground , it’s called a meteorite. 
 News: LM 
 Teghaza 001 FAQs
 Q1: What is Teghaza 001?
 Ans: It is a rose-coloured meteorite.
 Q2: Where was Teghaza 001 discovered?
 Ans: In the Sahara Desert, near the Teghaza salt plain in Mali.
 Q3: Why is Teghaza 001 considered scientifically significant among Martian meteorites?
 Ans: It is considered one of the three most ancient Martian meteorite samples discovered on Earth.
 Q4: How old is Teghaza 001 estimated to be?
 Ans: More than 4.1 billion years.
 Chidambaram Sabanayagar Temple: Madras HC Forms 5-Member Management Board 
 November 3, 2026 
 Chidambaram Sabanayagar Temple Latest News 
 The Madras High Court recently appointed a five-member Board of Management to take charge of the Chidambaram Sabanayagar Temple, citing alleged “maladministration” by the Podhu Dikshitars, a hereditary community of priests who had been entrusted with the temple's administration by the Supreme Court in 2014. 
 About Chidambaram Sabanayagar Temple 
 The Great Chidambaram Temple, also known as the Thillai Nataraja Temple or Sri Sabanayagar Temple, is a Hindu temple located in the temple town of Chidambaram in the Cuddalore district of Tamil Nadu. 
 It is dedicated to Nataraja , the cosmic dance form of Lord Shiva.    
 Chidambaram Sabanayagar Temple History 
 Historical evidence suggests a Shiva shrine existed at the site well before the 7th century AD, when the town was referred to as Thillai.  
 The Chola dynasty , who revered Nataraja as their family deity, significantly contributed to the temple's construction and enhancement during the 10th century.  
 It was during this period that the Chola king, Parantaka I, established the temple's golden roof.  
 Notable rulers such as Rajaraja Chola I, Kulothunga Chola I, Kundavai II, the daughter of Rajaraja Chola, and Vikrama Chola made considerable offerings to the shrine during its flourishing era.  
 Following the 10th century, the temple underwent various phases of damage, repair, renovation, and expansion throughout the 2nd millennium.  
 The majority of the temple's existing layout, architectural features , and structural elements date back to the late 12th and early 13th centuries, with subsequent additions made in a similar architectural style.  
 Over the years, numerous kingdoms, including the Viyanagara Rulers, Madurai Nayakas, Maharaja of Pudukkottai, Sethupathy , and even the British , have made donations to the temple.   
 The Podhu Dikshidars, a hereditary community of priests, have been managing the temple for centuries , unlike most of the other famous and historic temples. 
 Chidambaram Sabanayagar Temple Architecture 
 Covering an expansive area of 40 acres, the temple stands as a remarkable testament to the brilliance of Chola architecture.  
 This site holds considerable scientific significance, as it is positioned at the world's Magnetic Equator.  
 The temple complex is embedded inside four prakarams (courtyards), each surrounded by walls.  
 There are nine prominent gopurams that link the various courtyards.  
 The innermost structures , including the sanctum and the shrines, are designed with square layouts, and the roof of the sanctum sanctorum is adorned with gold plates.  
 The temple's wall carvings depict all 108 karanas from the Natya Shastra, authored by Bharata Muni , which serve as the foundational postures for Bharatanatyam, a classical Indian dance form.  
 The temple comprises five principal Halls or Sabhas: the Kanaka Sabha, the Chit Sabha, the Nritta Sabha, the Deva Sabha, and the Raja Sabha.  
 News: DH 
 Chidambaram Sabanayagar Temple FAQs
 Q1: Where is Chidambaram Sabanayagar Temple located?
 Ans: Chidambaram town, Cuddalore district, Tamil Nadu.
 Q2: What are the alternative names of Chidambaram Sabanayagar Temple?
 Ans: Thillai Nataraja Temple and the Great Chidambaram Temple.
 Q3: To which Hindu deity is Chidambaram Sabanayagar Temple dedicated?
 Ans: Lord Shiva, worshipped in his cosmic dance form as Nataraja.
 Q4: Which dynasty made significant contributions to the construction and development of Chidambaram Sabanayagar Temple?
 Ans: The Chola dynasty.
 Q5: Which hereditary community of priests has traditionally managed Chidambaram Sabanayagar Temple?
 Ans: The Podhu Dikshidars, a hereditary community of priests, have been managing the temple for centuries.
 Radhanagari Wildlife Sanctuary Records First Documented Tiger Sighting by Tourists 
 November 3, 2026 
 Radhanagari Wildlife Sanctuary Latest News 
 Tourists visiting Maharashtra’s Radhanagari-Dajipur Wildlife Sanctuary recently spotted a male Bengal tiger, marking the first officially documented tiger sighting captured on camera by tourists in the sanctuary.  
 About Radhanagari Wildlife Sanctuary 
 It is located in Maharashtra’s Kolhapur district.  
 Nestled in the southern end of the Sahyadri hills in the Western Ghats , it was the former hunting ground of the Maharaja of Kolhapur.   
 It was declared as a wildlife sanctuary in 1958 and is the first declared wildlife sanctuary in Maharashtra. 
 It was specially created for the conservation of the Indian bison (Gaur). 
 The sanctuary is also called ‘ Dajipur Wildlife Sanctuary’ and ‘Bison Sanctuary’.  
 It spans over 350 sq. km. of dense forest, grasslands, and hilly terrain.   
 The rivers that flow across the sanctuary are Bhogavati, Kallamma, Dudhganga, Dirba, and Tulshi , which then join the Krishna River. 
 At its heart lies the scenic Radhanagari Dam on the Bhogawati River, which plays a vital role in maintaining the forest ecosystem.  
 Flora :  
 It contains tropical evergreen forests typical of the northern Western Ghats.  
 The main flora found here are Ain, Anjani, Amba, Awala, Bhoma, Bibba, Chandala, Gela, Hirda, Jambul, Jambha, Kinjal, Kumbha, Katak, Nana, Pisa, Umbar, etc.  
 Fauna:   
 The Indian Bison is the flagship species of the area.  
 Besides, one can also spot leopards, sloth bears, tigers, barking deer, mouse deer, sambar, giant squirrels, and wild dogs.  
 It is also designated as an Important Bird Area by BirdLife International. 
 It is home to the rare and globally threatened Nilgiri wood-pigeon, along with Ceylon frogmouth, yellow-browed bulbul, dusky eagle-owl, Malabar grey hornbill, and great pied hornbill, and one of India's most admired songbirds, the Malabar whistling thrush. 
 News: TOI 
 Radhanagari Wildlife Sanctuary FAQs
 Q1: Where is Radhanagari Wildlife Sanctuary located?
 Ans: Kolhapur district, Maharashtra.
 Q2: What are the alternative names of Radhanagari Wildlife Sanctuary?
 Ans: Dajipur Wildlife Sanctuary and Bison Sanctuary.
 Q3: Which rivers flow through Radhanagari Wildlife Sanctuary?
 Ans: The rivers that flow across the sanctuary are Bhogavati, Kallamma, Dudhganga, Dirba, and Tulshi, which then join the Krishna River.
 Q4: What type of forests are predominantly found in Radhanagari Wildlife Sanctuary?
 Ans: Tropical evergreen forests.
 Q5: Which animal is the flagship species of Radhanagari Wildlife Sanctuary?
 Ans: Indian bison (Gaur).
 Project 28A: India Signs ₹53,866 Crore Deal for 8 Next Generation Corvettes 
 November 3, 2026 
 Project 28A Latest News 
 The Ministry of Defence recently signed contracts worth ₹53,866.50 crore with two state-owned shipyards for eight Next Generation Corvettes (NGCs) for the Navy under Project 28A. 
 About Project 28A 
 It is the Indian Navy’s Next Generation Corvettes (NGCs) programme. 
 Under the contracts, Garden Reach Shipbuilders & Engineers Limited (GRSE), Kolkata, will construct five corvettes, while Goa Shipyard Limited (GSL) will construct the remaining three. 
 It is the first project in which the ships will be indigenously designed by the Indian Navy and constructed by Defence Public Sector Undertakings (DPSUs) selected through a competitive process. 
 A corvette in the Indian Navy is a small , fast, and heavily armed warship ranked just below a frigate in size.  
 NGCs are designed for multi-role operations, including offensive Ship-to-Ship or Ship-to-Surface Missile Attacks, Anti-Missile Defences, Anti-Submarine Warfare Operations, Escort Dutie s, Maritime Interdiction Operations (MIO) including Visit Board Search and Seizure, and Local Naval Defence.  
 The Indian Navy currently operates 18 to 24 corvettes in active service.  
 Features of Next Generation Corvettes (NGCs) 
 These warships will be 127 metres long and 17.6 metres wide.  
 They will have a deadweight tonnage of 4,950 tonnes , with the capability of operating at sea without replenishment for 14 days.  
 The NGCs will accommodate 11 officers and 139 sailors.  
 The platforms will have a highly sophisticated propulsion architecture of a Combined Diesel and Gas turbine with a Cross-Connect gearbox (CODAG-CC), driving two Controllable Pitch Propellers (CPP).  
 Their maximum speed will be 26 knots.  
 The warships will be fitted with advanced weapons and navigation suites. 
 The proposed systems include Medium Range Anti-Ship Missiles , Medium Range Surface-to-Air Missiles (MRSAM) and 324 mm torpedo tubes.  
 The armament suite will also include an OTO Melara 76 mm Super Rapid Gun Mount (SRGM) with the latest upgrade, an AK-630 Close-In Weapon System (CIWS) and 12.7 mm Stabilised Remote-Controlled Guns (SRCGs) integrated with an Electro-Optic-based Fire Control System (EOFCS). 
 The sensor suite will include an Electro-Optical Infrared Search and Track (EOIRST) system and a Multi-Function Surveillance, Track, and Guidance Radar (MFSTAR). 
 The NGCs will also carry helicopters. 
 News: SENT 
 Project 28A FAQs
 Q1: What is Project 28A?
 Ans: The Indian Navy’s Next Generation Corvettes (NGCs) programme.
 Q2: How many corvettes will be constructed under Project 28A?
 Ans: Eight.
 Q3: What is the significance of Project 28A in terms of warship design and construction?
 Ans: It is the first project in which the ships will be indigenously designed by the Indian Navy and constructed by Defence Public Sector Undertakings (DPSUs) selected through a competitive process.
 Q4: Which organisation is responsible for constructing five of the eight corvettes under Project 28A?
 Ans: Garden Reach Shipbuilders & Engineers Limited (GRSE), Kolkata.
 Q5: Which shipyard will construct the remaining three corvettes under Project 28A?
 Ans: Goa Shipyard Limited (GSL).
 Asia-Pacific Broadcasting Union: Prasar Bharati Wins Two Honours at ABU Prizes 2026 
 November 3, 2026 
 Asia-Pacific Broadcasting Union Latest News 
 Prasar Bharati has received two major recognitions at the Asia-Pacific Broadcasting Union Prizes 2026, held in Colombo. 
 About Asia-Pacific Broadcasting Union 
 It is a not-for-profit, non-governmental organisation established in 1964. 
 It is dedicated to advancing broadcasting and media cooperation across the Asia-Pacific. 
 It connects around 224 organisations across 66 countries, reaching audiences across half the globe. 
 It serves as a central platform where members share content, exchange ideas, and collectively navigate the challenges shaping the future of media. 
 Participants: It consists of 224 members in 66 countries. 
 Headquarter: Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia 
 Governance of Asia-Pacific Broadcasting Union 
 General Assembly 
 It is the supreme body of the ABU and, subject to the provisions of the Statutes, has all the powers necessary to achieve the objectives of the ABU. 
 It comprises all the Full, Additional Full, and Associate members of the Union. 
 Administrative Council 
 The ABU’s “board of directors” is called the Administrative Council. 
 It consists of 18 of its Full and Additional Full members, who are elected by the members at the annual General Assembly for a three-year term. 
 The council meets twice-yearly to decide on policy matters, review the Union’s finances and consider current issues facing the Union. 
 Source: DD News 
 Asia-Pacific Broadcasting Union FAQs
 Q1: Where is Asia-Pacific Broadcasting Union located ?
 Ans: Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia
 Q2: What is Asia-Pacific Broadcasting Union?
 Ans: It is a not-for-profit, non-governmental organisation established in 1964.
 Bupleurum oslaense: New Himalayan Plant Species Discovered in Uttarakhand, Critically Endangered 
 November 3, 2026 
 Bupleurum Oslaense Latest News 
 Recently, botanists from the Botanical Survey of India have discovered and described a brand-new plant species, named Bupleurum oslaense. 
 About Bupleurum Oslaense 
 It is a new plant species discovered in the temperate forests of the Western Himalayas. 
 It is a new member of the family Apiaceae. 
 It shares genetic and structural similarities with Bupleurum petiolulatum (a relative native to China). 
 It was found at an elevation of roughly 2,550 meters within the Govind Pashu Vihar National Park and Sanctuary in Uttarakhand, India. 
 Features 
 It is standing up to 80 centimetres tall with a sturdy, stout habit. 
 It features narrower lower leaves, broader upper leaves with distinct red-tinged margins, larger bracts numbering between three and five, and flower clusters (umbellules) packing 10 to 20 flowers each. 
 Consequently, following strict International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN) guidelines, this species has been formally assessed and categorised as "Critically Endangered." 
 Source: RM 
 Bupleurum Oslaense FAQs
 Q1: What is Bupleurum Oslaense?
 Ans: New Plant species
 Q2: Where was Bupleurum Oslaense discovered?
 Ans: Western Himalayas
 Pradhan Mantri Jeevan Jyoti Bima Yojana: J&K Records 13.07 Lakh Enrolments 
 November 3, 2026 
 Pradhan Mantri Jeevan Jyoti Bima Yojana Latest News 
 The Pradhan Mantri Jeevan Jyoti Bima Yojana (PMJJBY) has recorded 13.07 lakh cumulative enrolments across Jammu and Kashmir, strengthening access to affordable life insurance and financial security for families across the Union Territory. 
 About Pradhan Mantri Jeevan Jyoti Bima Yojana 
 It is a flagship life insurance scheme launched by the Government of India to provide affordable life insurance coverage to the economically weaker sections of society. 
 It was launched in May 2015 under the Ministry of Finance. 
 It aims to increase access to life insurance across the country. It offers a one-year life insurance policy, renewable every year. 
 Read more about: PMJJBY 
 Features of Pradhan Mantri Jeevan Jyoti Bima Yojana 
 Life Cover: Under PMJJBY, a life insurance cover of ₹2 lakh is provided in case of death of the insured due to any reason, natural or accidental. 
 Premium Amount: ₹436 per annum (auto-debited from bank account). 
 Eligibility: Indian citizens aged between 18 and 50 years. 
 Renewal: Annual renewal up to the age of 55 years. 
 Risk Coverage: Covers death due to both natural and accidental causes. 
 Implementing Agencies: Public and private sector life insurance companies in tie-up with banks. 
 Source: News On Air 
 Pradhan Mantri Jeevan Jyoti Bima Yojana FAQs
 Q1: What is the aim of Pradhan Mantri Jeevan Jyoti Bima Yojana?
 Ans: It aims to increase access to life insurance across the country.
 Q2: What is the premium amount of Pradhan Mantri Jeevan Jyoti Bima Yojana?
 Ans: ₹436 per annum (auto-debited from bank account).
 Exercise Tiger Triumph 2026: India and US Complete 5th Joint Disaster Relief Drill 
 November 3, 2026 
 Exercise Tiger Triumph 2026 Latest News 
 The United States and Indian Armed Forces have commenced the fifth edition of the bilateral exercise Tiger Triumph 2026 in Visakhapatnam. 
 About Exercise Tiger Triumph 2026 
 It is an India-U.S. tri-service Humanitarian Assistance and Disaster Relief (HADR) Exercise . 
 It is aimed at strengthening defence cooperation , enhancing operational interoperability and improving their ability to respond jointly to regional crises and natural disasters. 
 The exercise reflects the deepening convergence of India–US strategic maritime interests and the growing defence partnership between the two nations. 
 Participating Units from India 
 From the Indian side include specialists from all domains of maritime operations from the Indian Navy, ground forces from the Indian Army and representatives from various units of the Indian Air Force, as well as Special Forces personnel from all three Services. 
 A team from the NDRF will also participate for the first time in the 5th edition of Tiger Triumph 2026. 
 Source: PIB 
 Exercise Tiger Triumph 2026 FAQs
 Q1: What is Exercise Tiger Triumph 2026?
 Ans: It is an India-U.S. tri-service Humanitarian Assistance and Disaster Relief (HADR) Exercise.
 Q2: What is the aim of Exercise Tiger Triumph?
 Ans: It is aimed at strengthening defence cooperation, enhancing operational interoperability and improving their ability to respond jointly to regional crises and natural disasters.
 Asiatic Black Bear: 2,357 Attacks Reported in Kashmir Over 20 Years 
 November 3, 2026 
 Asiatic Black Bear Latest News 
 Recently, researchers from Wildlife Institute of India (WII ) have documented what they describe as the first verified photographic evidence of an Asiatic black bear (Ursus thibetanus) preying on an endangered red panda (Ailurus fulgens). 
 About Asiatic Black Bear 
 It is a medium-sized bear species native to Asia . 
 It is unique among bears in that it is largely adapted to an arboreal lifestyle. 
 Appearance: Its fur is black with a “V” shape of light beige to white on its chest, a small beige to white crescent on its throat, and a small white spot on its chin. 
 Habitat: The species prefers heavily forested broadleaved and coniferous forest as habitat.  It uses orchards, agricultural fields and human habitation to move between forest patches. 
 Distribution: It is found in Bangladesh, Bhutan, Cambodia, China, India, Iran, Japan and South Korea 
 In India, they are found across Himalayan ranges from eastern to western side at an altitude between 2,600-ft and 11,400-ft above sea level. 
 Diet: They are omnivores that normally feed on berries, cherries, acorns, insects, squirrels and frogs, and typically hibernate from late Nov to March. 
 They are excellent climbers and swimmers, often seen foraging on fruit trees or near rivers. 
 Threats: It is threatened by deforestation and poaching for its body parts, which are used in traditional medicine. 
 Conservation status 
 IUCN Red List: Vulnerable 
 CITES: Appendix I 
 Wild Life Protection Act 1972: Schedule II 
 Source: TOI 
 Asiatic Black Bear FAQs
 Q1: Where do we find Asiatic Black Bear ?
 Ans: It is found in Bangladesh, Bhutan, Cambodia, China, India, Iran, Japan and South Korea
 Q2: What is the IUCN status of Asiatic Black Bear ?
 Ans: Vulnerable (VU)
 Mayon Volcano Eruption in Philippines Forces Thousands to Evacuate 
 November 3, 2026 
 Mayon Volcano Latest News 
 One of the most active volcanoes in the Philippines, Mayon, fired a dark column of ash over thousands of metres into the sky in a "moderately explosive eruption" recently. 
 About Mayon Volcano 
 It is an active volcano located in Albay province on Luzon Island in the Philippines . 
 It is a stratovolcano , that is, it is made out of alternating strata of lava and ash and is part of the Ring of Fire in the Pacific Ocean.   
 It is located on the eastern side of Luzon, beside the Philippine Trench, which is the convergent boundary where the Philippine Sea Plate is driven under the Philippine Mobile Belt.  
 Rising to 2462 m above the Albay Gulf, it is the P hilippines’ most active volcano.  
 Celebrated as one of the most symmetrical volcanic cones on Earth , it has a base 130 km in circumference and has steep upper slopes. 
 Right at the very peak sits a circular volcanic crater that measures about 250 m (820 ft) across.  
 Popular with climbers and campers, the volcano is the centre of Mayon Volcano National Park. UNESCO named it an official biosphere reserve in 2016.  
 There are large abaca plantations on its lower slopes.  
 Historical eruptions date back to 1616 CE that have been characterized by Strombolian eruptions, lava flows , pyroclastic flows, and mudflows.  
 There have been more than 30 eruptions recorded since 1616.    
 Mayon’s most violent eruption, in 1814, killed more than 1200 people and devastated several towns.  
 An eruption in 1993 caused 79 deaths.  
 Eruptions occur predominately from the central conduit and have also produced lava flows that travel far down the flanks. 
 News: WION 
 Mayon Volcano FAQs
 Q1: Where is Mayon Volcano located?
 Ans: Albay province, Luzon Island, Philippines.
 Q2: What type of volcano is Mayon Volcano?
 Ans: Stratovolcano (composite volcano).
 Q3: Which tectonic plate boundary is associated with Mayon Volcano?
 Ans: A convergent plate boundary.
 Q4: For which distinctive geographical feature is Mayon Volcano particularly famous?
 Ans: Its remarkably symmetrical, near-perfect conical shape.
